headline: New law lets the VA step in to help veterans avoid foreclosure on VA-backed home loans and boosts funding for homeless veteran programs.
what_it_does: The VA can pay a lender the amount needed to stop a foreclosure on a VA-guaranteed home loan, in exchange for a secured interest in the home. It creates a five-year Partial Claim Program in which the VA can buy part of the debt on a primary home that is behind on payments or close to it, and requires the VA to set loss mitigation steps lenders must follow first. The VA must also report to Congress on making sure VA loan buyers are not disadvantaged when seeking a real estate agent. It temporarily raises authorized funding for the VA's Grant and Per Diem program for homeless veterans.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans with VA-guaranteed home loans who are behind on payments
who_it_affects.how: They may get VA help to avoid foreclosure, but they owe the VA for any loss if they later default on a loan the VA partly paid off.

who_it_affects.group: Banks and companies that hold or service VA-guaranteed home loans
who_it_affects.how: They must follow VA loss mitigation steps in order and may receive VA payments to resolve loans in default.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans buying homes with VA loans
who_it_affects.how: The VA must report on how to keep them from being disadvantaged when trying to hire a real estate agent or broker.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans experiencing homelessness and the public or nonprofit groups that serve them
who_it_affects.how: More money is authorized for the Grant and Per Diem program, which funds housing and support services, for fiscal years 2025 and 2026.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted July 30, 2025; the Partial Claim Program runs for five years, and the homeless program funding increase covers FY2025 and FY2026.
